stem: Two concentrated fertilizer components are combined directly and a visible precipitate forms before final dilution. What is the strongest response?
choices: Apply the mixture after completing the normal dilution, because visible solids in concentrate are expected to redissolve once enough water is added and therefore do not affect final nutrient availability
Continue mixing until the solids become smaller, then use the solution if final EC matches target, because target EC confirms that the precipitated ions remain available
Stop and verify compatible mixing and dilution procedures before using the solution, because precipitation can remove ions from the dissolved nutrient supply
Correct the final solution pH and use it if pH and EC are within target, treating the precipitate as a cosmetic mixing issue rather than a change in dissolved nutrient chemistry
rationale: Some concentrated fertilizer components can react and precipitate when combined improperly. Mixing and dilution procedures should prevent incompatible concentrates from forming insoluble compounds before application.
